Subject: POC: Prompt dataset & eval plan — next steps

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff:

1) Success criteria (what Acme needs to validate):
  - 85% precision on intent extraction for billing/returns tickets (measured on a holdout set you provide)
  - <500ms 95th percentile latency for single-turn ticket classification in our dedicated setup
  - End-to-end accuracy for automated reply suggestions >= 75% as judged by your CS team

2) What we need from Acme to run the evaluation:
  - Prompt set: examples of user messages and the top-1 expected assistant response/label (CSV or JSONL). Ideally 1,000–3,000 rows; minimum 200 representative prompts to start.
  - Chat logs (anonymized): 2–4 weeks of chat logs for typical usage patterns (timestamps, user messages, agent responses) — ZIP or S3 link.
  - Any existing evaluation scripts or specific edge cases you want prioritized.

3) Proposed plan & timeline:
  - 3/22: PoC kickoff + data handoff (your team shares files or Drive link)
  - 3/23–3/29: Ingest, normalization, and baseline run on Redwood hosted POC environment
  - 3/30–4/05: Iteration with model/config tweaks + evaluation reports
  - 4/06: Demo to Acme stakeholders, review results and next-step recommendations

4) Ownership / points of contact:
  - Marissa Cole (AE) — overall program & timeline owner
  - Rishi Malhotra (SE) — technical lead, ingestion and eval config
  - Monica Patel (CS) — rollout and success criteria alignment

Can you confirm the timeline works and share the minimum prompt set and any chat logs by EOD 3/22? If you prefer, S3 or Drive links are fine.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — happy to own ingestion & baseline. A few technical notes / asks so we can estimate effort:

1) CSV/JSONL format: we prefer a CSV with headers: id, user_message, expected_label, expected_response (expected_response optional). If Acme's CSV differs we can provide a small Python script to normalize.
2) Anonymization: ideally replace PII with placeholders (e.g., <NAME>, <EMAIL>). If they cannot, we can run a redaction pass but will need a signed data processing addendum — Monica, ping for DPA process?
3) Sample size: for the baseline run we'll ingest a random 500 prompts first to validate parsing and metrics, then scale to full set.
4) Logs: compressed JSONL or ZIP with columns: timestamp, user_message, agent_response, conversation_id. We do not need full agent internal notes.

I’ll prepare the normalization script and a short README. Posting here as an attachment: poc_eval_template.xlsx (includes expected headers & eval metric definitions).

Next steps for me:
- Share normalization script & README by EOD 3/21
- Run baseline on 500 prompts within 48 hours of handoff
